correctness.rationale: Two exact primal triangular-cap subtractions and two polar convex-hull triangles give M=(n-2+2/h)(n sin²(pi/n)-2(1-h)²). The explicit derivative numerator G has G(c)>0 and G(1)<0, and G is strictly decreasing on (c,1) for every even n≥6; n=4 reduces to a concave quadratic. This proves the unique interior maximum, endpoint classification, and all quantifiers. Expansion of the unique root and of the regular polygon product yields the sharp 3/8 asymptotic fraction. The standalone independent polygon/facet computation passed 629 checks, but the proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: Meyer–Reisner (2011) optimizes over all polygons of bounded vertex count, but not along this constrained antipodal cutting path. Lin–Leng (2010) studies vertex deletion for the Mahler minimum without the nonmonotone intermediate path. Meyer–Reisner (2006) establishes broad shadow-system results, and Alexander–Fradelizi–Zvavitch (2017) maximizes over all polygons. None of the investigated primary arguments states or directly entails the exact two-cap product, the unique strict interior maximizer, and the 3/8 asymptotic comparison. Targeted actual searches returned no matching claim. Historical priority beyond the inspected record remains uncertain.

value.rationale: A natural geometry operation simultaneously decreases primal area and increases polar area, so its total Mahler-product response is not a textbook monotonicity deduction. Classification for every even polygon order discovers a unique interior optimum and a sharp 3/8 proportion of the regular (n+2)-vertex benchmark as n grows. The exact quantitative optimum is a usable comparison test for bounded-complexity symmetric convex deformations, even without a theorem for arbitrary polygons.
